summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and multiple airway reconstructions was admitted for pain when swallowing, which she described as dull at baseline and sharp with swallowing. She had recently been hospitalized for pain and fluid resuscitation with a negative infectious workup. On admission, she was mildly lightheaded due to poor oral intake, which resolved with IV fluids. Evaluation by ENT and interventional pulmonology, including fiberoptic exam, showed no infection or structural abnormality but noted marked crusting in the airway. Pain was initially managed with IV hydromorphone and transitioned to oral hydromorphone, acetaminophen, naproxen, and viscous lidocaine. She tolerated a regular diet, pain improved, and she was discharged home with a one-week course of oral pain medications and instructions to follow up with her PCP, pulmonologist, and ENT.
problems: Other diseases of trachea and bronchus
